statement: Finite fixed-channel graphs fail full zeta counting growth; an infinite disconnected butterfly collection can match oscillatory coefficients but loses finite mean density and local spectral finiteness. Together they identify a precise missing simultaneous requirement: controlled full spectral mass plus arithmetic trace matching.
compatible_assumptions: Separate finite fixed-model and infinite-collection statements; no illegal application of finite bound to infinite object.
already_proved: finite graph no-go; authors explicit divergent-mean limitation for butterfly collection
conjectural_part: a connected finite-mass infinite graph with correct arithmetic trace identity is not supplied
next_step: Prove a local spectral mass bound and self-adjoint domain for a proposed connected/reused graph before coefficient matching.
counterexamples: The butterfly construction itself shows that oscillatory matching alone does not imply full spectral identification.
tests: Compute positive smoothed spectral mass before subtracting any mean; track both cutoff and smoothing dependence.
significance: precise model-design obstacle; no RH proof
verification_status: source-supported synthesis; not a novelty claim
